newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO REJECTS CHARGES OF MASSIVE MONEY LAUNDERING.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO REJECTS CHARGES OF MASSIVE MONEY LAUNDERING.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Ministry on Wednesday rejected allegations that Mexican businesses and financial institutions were laundering large amounts of illegal cash, thus boosting the economy.

An article published this week in the magazine Latin Trade said that cash worth between $10 billion to $15 billion per year was being laundered through Mexico, equivalent to 3.0 to 5.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

"We consider them (the allegations) to be irresponsible because we have not been able to see any objective sources make these estimations," Finance Ministry spokesman Alejandro Valenzuela told a news conference.
"Amounts worth 5.0 percent of GDP could not pass unnoticed."

He acknowledged that money laundering was a problem in Mexico and internationally and said the government has introduced measures to combat the practice. ((--Robert Kozak, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 9559))
